SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
CONFIDENTIAL REPORT
File No............
8739
18/9/38
20 9 38
Date September 19th 38

Subject Communication dated 25-8-38 from the British Consulate-General
concerning Mr. V.S. Prisiajnikoff-Vale.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by C. Gasford. S.I.

* Au alo
D 8564

Valentin Sergeyevich PRISIAJNIKOFF-VALE, Russian, born
on June 22, 1903 at Tomsk, Siberia. According to his own state-
ment, he graduated from a commercial school in Omsk in 1919, after
which he attended the local Institute for Agriculture for about
3 years. In 1922 he arrived in Shanghai from Russia together
with his mother and sister and has since been residing in this
city.

Here he is reported to have been employed for diffe-
rent periods with various local newspapers and commercial firms
including the newspapers " New Shanghai Time" (1923), "Novoye
Slovo" (1924), the Barabash Co, Oriental Press, Ave. Edward VII
(1925-1926), Asia Press, Avenue Joffre (1927) and Marden Transport
Co. (1928). From 1929 to 1932 he worked as a journalist in the
Russian newspaper "Slovo", after which he published his own weekly
magazine entitled "PROJECTOR" for about four years. In 1936 he
re-joined the newspaper "Slovo" and from September, 1937 has been
holding the post of an editor in this paper.

Prisiajnikoff is the author of a couple of books of
fiction and has been participating in the activities of the lo-
cal Russian literary circle known as "Ponedelnik". It appears
that "Vale" is his pen name.

He was married to one Miss S.G. Moszepan, but divorced
her several years ago. One of his sisters is married to Sergeant
M.K. Fedoroff of the Shanghai Municipal Police, and the other,
who is also married, is reported to be residing in England at
present together with her mother.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee
118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Shanghai City Government Po-
lice Bureau (Reg. 4533).

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特务科第一股
机密报告
档案号............
8739
18/9/38
20 9 38
日期：1938年9月19日

事由：英国总领事馆于1938年8月25日来函，涉及 V.S. Prisiajnikoff-Vale 先生。
由 D.S.I. Prokofiev 撰写。由 S.I. C. Gasford 转呈。

* Au alo
D 8564

瓦连京·谢尔盖耶维奇·普里西亚日尼科夫-瓦列（Valentin Sergeyevich PRISIAJNIKOFF-VALE），俄国人，1903年6月22日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克。据其自述，他于1919年毕业于鄂木斯克的一所商业学校，随后在当地农业学院就读约3年。1922年，他与母亲及妹妹从俄国抵达上海，此后一直居住在该市。

据报，他在上海期间曾受雇于当地多家报社及商行，任期长短不一，包括《新上海时报》（New Shanghai Time，1923年）、《新词报》（Novoye Slovo，1924年）、巴拉巴什公司（Barabash Co）、东方出版社（Oriental Press，爱多亚路，1925-1926年）、亚洲出版社（Asia Press，霞飞路，1927年）以及马登运输公司（Marden Transport Co.，1928年）。1929年至1932年间，他在俄文报纸《言论报》（Slovo）担任记者，随后创办并出版了一份名为《探照灯》（PROJECTOR）的周刊，历时约四年。1936年，他重新加入《言论报》，并自1937年9月起在该报担任编辑职务。

普里西亚日尼科夫是几本小说的作者，并参与了当地名为“星期一”（Ponedelnik）的俄罗斯文学团体的活动。“瓦列”（Vale）似乎是他的笔名。

他曾与 S.G. Moszepan 小姐结婚，但数年前已离婚。他的一个妹妹嫁给了上海公共租界工部局警务处的警长 M.K. Fedoroff；另一个妹妹也已婚，据报目前与其母亲一同居住在英格兰。

他在莫尔缅路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记注册，并在上海市政府警察局登记（注册号 4533）。
